should be [144:3-4]; [source_identity] "Ps 144,1" vs "Ps 144,1": LXX Ps 144:1 corresponds to Hebrew/English Ps 145:1, not Ps 144:1; should be [145:1]; [source_identity] "Ps 144,4" vs "Ps 144,4": LXX Ps 144:4 corresponds to Hebrew/English Ps 145:4, not Ps 144:4; should be [145:4]; [completeness] "In the present life these words could apply to one human being after another in succession" vs "Κατὰ μὲν τὸν νῦν βίον τοῦ κατὰ διαδοχὴν ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ταῦτα ἂν εἶναι δύναιτο": Missing 'of-the according-to-succession one human-being' genitive construction; 'these words' adds 'words' not in source; [agency] "the worshiper adds" vs "προστίθεται": Subject is impersonal 'it is added' or he/psalmist adds, not specifically 'the worshiper'; [completeness] "seeing that they receive praise beyond all praise" vs "ὑπὲρ πάντα ἔπαινον τυγχάνοντα αὐτὰ ὁρῶσα": Misconstrued: 'obtaining them beyond all praise seeing' — the generation sees the works obtaining praise beyond all praise, not 'they receive praise' | part 2/2: [agency] "your power and wisdom is your only-begotten Son" vs "δύναμις δὲ καὶ σοφία σου τὸ γέννημα τὸ μονογενές σου": Greek has 'your power and wisdom [is] your offspring the only-begotten'; English adds 'Son' not in source; [modality] "since humans are not yet able to receive it" vs "οὔπω τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐχόντων δεκτικῶς": Greek 'not yet of humans having [it] receptively' is participial, not 'able to receive'; [agency] "therefore he adds what is fitting for God" vs "διὸ ἐπιφέρει τὸ πρέπον θεῷ": Subject of ἐπιφέρει is the psalmist/speaker, not 'he' referring to God; ambiguous reference; [completeness] "for created things" vs "τῶν δημιουργουμένων": Greek 'of the being-created things' is substantival/partitive with 'foods', not modifier of 'food'
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: completeness, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/2: [scripture] "according to Ecclesiastes" vs "κατὰ τὸν Ἐκκλησιαστήν": Source cites Ecclesiastes but the preceding quotation is from Isaiah; reference mismatch with content. | part 2/2: [completeness] "but likening the creative power in this way." vs "ἀλλὰ τὸ δημιουργικὸν οὕτως ὁμοιῶν": Drops the article τὸ: 'the creative power' becomes 'creative power'; also 'thus' (οὕτως) modifies the likening, not 'in this way' as separate phrase.
Latin quote (from model note, verified): «Κατὰ μὲν τὸν νῦν βίον τοῦ κατὰ διαδοχὴν ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ταῦτα ἂν εἶναι δύναιτο»
English quote (from model note, verified): «according to Ecclesiastes»
ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): Checked each flag against the Greek; none is a meaning error. Fragment headings (Ps 143,4.5; 144,1; 144,4) are the edition's LXX lemmata. 'these words' supplies the subject of ταῦτα. προστίθεται 'is added' is rendered with its implied agent (the one praising). ὑπὲρ πάντα ἔπαινον τυγχάνοντα αὐτὰ ὁρῶσα = seeing them obtain (praise) beyond all praise, as rendered. τὸ γέννημα τὸ μονογενές σου = your only-begotten offspring; 'Son' is the referent, confirmed by the next clause (Χριστὸς θεοῦ δύναμις καὶ θεοῦ σοφία). The rest are participle style.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): Not meaning errors. κατὰ τὸν Ἐκκλησιαστήν is right: 'everything God made remains forever' is Ecclesiastes 3:14 (πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός, αὐτὰ ἔσται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα), not Isaiah. 'likening the creative power in this way' keeps τὸ δημιουργικὸν and οὕτως.
